findings.title: assignment_source_dict contains a datetime, which is not JSON-serializable for Celery
findings.body: sync_group_assignee_outbound enqueues sync_assignee_outbound with 'assignment_source_dict': assignment_source.to_dict(). AssignmentSource.to_dict() uses dataclasses.asdict(), so the dict includes the 'queued' field as a datetime.datetime instance. Sentry's Celery tasks use JSON serialization, so publishing this message raises TypeError/kombu EncodeError ('Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable') at apply_async time. This fires on exactly the path this PR adds: every inbound webhook assignment/deassignment now carries an AssignmentSource, so the first apply_async call in the loop raises, no outbound syncs are enqueued (including to other integrations, which the PR says should still propagate), and the exception propagates through GroupAssignee.assign()/deassign() back to the webhook handler, producing 500s and webhook retries. The new tests don't catch this because self.tasks() runs tasks eagerly without message serialization. Fix by removing the unused 'queued' field or serializing it (e.g., isoformat()) in to_dict and parsing it back in from_dict.

findings.title: queued default is evaluated once at module import time
findings.body: In the AssignmentSource dataclass, 'queued: datetime = timezone.now()' is evaluated a single time when the class is defined, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit queued value (including ones rebuilt by from_dict when the key is absent) shares the same timestamp from process start, not the time the source was actually created. The correct pattern is field(default_factory=timezone.now). Although nothing consumes 'queued' yet, any future use (e.g., ignoring stale assignments) would silently operate on wrong data, and the existing test only asserts the value is not None so it cannot catch this.

findings.title: assignment_source added to the wrong abstract method contract
findings.body: The abstract IssueSyncIntegration.sync_status_outbound signature now declares 'assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None', but no caller ever passes it and no inbound status flow creates an AssignmentSource, so the parameter is dead and misleading (status sync cycles are not addressed by this PR). Conversely, sync_assignee_outbound in the task now always passes assignment_source=... to installation.sync_assignee_outbound, yet the abstract sync_assignee_outbound signature was not updated to declare it — concrete implementations only receive it incidentally via **kwargs, so anyone implementing or type-checking against the documented abstract contract won't know the argument exists. Add the parameter to sync_assignee_outbound's abstract signature and drop it from sync_status_outbound until status cycle-breaking is actually implemented.

findings.title: New task kwarg is enqueued in the same deploy it is accepted, risking TypeError on old workers
findings.body: The PR both adds the 'assignment_source_dict' parameter to the sync_assignee_outbound task and immediately starts sending it from sync_group_assignee_outbound. During a rolling deploy, messages produced by new code can be picked up by workers still running the old three-argument signature, which raises TypeError: sync_assignee_outbound() got an unexpected keyword argument 'assignment_source_dict'. TypeError is not in the @retry exclude list, so the message retries up to 5 times at 5-minute delays and is dropped if the deploy takes longer than ~25 minutes to reach all workers. The usual mitigation is to deploy the worker signature change first and enable the enqueueing side only after all workers accept the new kwarg (or gate it behind a flag).
